summary: This proposed standard clarifies the instructions given to IANA for the WebSocket subprotocol name registry that was set up by RFC 6455. It is a small administrative fix so that registrations are handled consistently.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7936 clarifies how IANA handles case in WebSocket subprotocol names. Names are matched with case sensitivity, but a name differing from an existing one only by case must be rejected.

subtitle: Clarifies case handling in the WebSocket subprotocol name registry.

tldr.problem: The WebSocket subprotocol registry needed clearer instructions for handling names that differ only by letter case.
tldr.mechanism: Tokens are matched case-sensitively, but IANA must decline a registration that differs from an existing name only by case.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7936 updates RFC 6455 with clarified registry procedures.

today: RFC 7936 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 6455. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Need for Clarification
sections.content: RFC 6455 created the WebSocket Subprotocol Name Registry and specified First Come First Served registration. As other protocols reused the registry, the instructions for case-sensitive names needed clarification. RFC 7936 explains the matching rule and the handling of names that differ only by case.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry needed a clear rule for uppercase and lowercase letters. This RFC states how names are compared and which registrations IANA must reject.

sections.title: How Names Are Compared
sections.content: Registered tokens are matched using case-sensitive string matching. However, IANA must decline a registration that differs from an existing registration only in case. The RFC encourages registrants to consult RFC 6455 Section 1.9 for advice on avoiding collisions.
sections.plainLanguage: Uppercase and lowercase letters are different when tokens are matched. IANA still refuses a new token if its only difference from an existing one is capitalization.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 7936 describes an update to registry policy, not a protocol. It adds the clarification to IANA's registration procedures and lists RFC 6455 as a reference for the registry.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC changes registry instructions. It does not define a protocol.
